title: AccuWeather Alert: Coastal low to mature overnight; snow north and west | Live update
text:
NYC weather: Coastal low picks up overnight, snow north & west Friday - ABC7 New York 
 24/7 Live New York City New Jersey Long Island Northern Suburbs Connecticut Live WEATHER 
 AccuWeather Alert: Coastal low to mature overnight; snow north and west | Live update 
 Stay with Eyewitness News and the AccuWeather team for continuing updates on the coastal low. 
 Stream New York's #1 news - AccuWeather - original content 24/7 Last updated: Friday, November 13, 2026 5:11AM GMT Share Follow abc7NY on Google NEW YORK (WABC) -- After a lull, rain will start to pick up again as the next coastal low matures and slides south to east, bringing with it a raw, windy Friday, and the potential for some snow accumulations to areas north and west of New York City.
 Temperatures will drop to around 42 overnight as a gusty northeast wind pulls in the coldest air of the season.
 The rain-snow line will move south and east through the Catskills and Poconos overnight.
 ACCUWEATHER ALERT CONTINUES FRIDAY
 Roads should stay wet rather than icy for the Friday morning commute, though slick spots and coatings on colder surfaces are possible well north and west of the city.
 Friday will be raw and windy, with rain and snow steadiest through early afternoon. Highs will be around 40, and it will feel like the 30s all day. New York City will mostly see rain, with another third of an inch to an inch possible. A few flakes could mix in, with the best chance in the Bronx, but no snow will stick in the city. The Catskills could see 1 to 3 inches.
 The precipitation tapers Friday afternoon, with a few lingering rain and snow showers Friday night.
 The weekend will be blustery and chilly, with highs in the mid-to-upper 40s.
